correctness.rationale: An explicitly parametrized 60-point Gaussian-integer coordinate set supplies the 60 dual plane normals; all 3600 orthogonality tests and 900 incidences are exact. A degree-six annihilating polynomial and six power traces determine the complete symmetric incidence spectrum, proving graph connectedness and Kirchhoff determinant. Two independently reduced 119x119 integer Laplacians give identical p-local Smith valuations for p=2,3,5,7 with moduli beyond all valuations; their exponents exactly match the independent determinant. The sorted valuation factors give a valid divisibility chain, recovering the complete finite critical group.

evidence: Tamimi (2022), The Sandpile & Smith Groups of Certain Classes of Graphs, describes selected graph families and partial strongly regular group results; no asserted universal theorem covers this six-eigenvalue bipartite graph.
The 120-Klein graph has Laplacian eigenvalues 0, 30, 12, 18, 10, 20, 14, 16 and is not a three-eigenvalue strongly regular graph.
No published-finding corpus hit had a general theorem implying exact invariant factors for all 120-Klein graph Laplacians.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing the ordinary graph spectrum or spanning-tree count fixes only the product of nonunit Smith factors, not their individual valuations. Selected strongly regular or circulant critical-group formulas do not determine this particular graph. Specific hidden parameter-covering theorems remain possible.

value.rationale: Klein’s historically distinguished projective 60-point/60-plane reflection configuration is a natural self-dual algebraic-geometric incidence, not an arbitrary selected subgraph. The complete 55-factor graph Jacobian is an integral divisor invariant inaccessible from rational spectral or 60_15 count data alone. Its exponent 201600, high 2-primary filtration and 7-rank 30 also determine the component group in a standard 120-component semistable stable-curve realization, providing a concrete exact reference for degeneration and integral graph calculations.
